title: VM/PageBacked v1 completion
summary: Bridge VM/PageBacked from current ~45% structure / ~30% behavior toward ~85% on both, leaving only items that the active design docs explicitly defer (rmap, hugetlb, userfaultfd, in-place mprotect, reclaim policy, writeback scheduling) or that depend on Process/ThreadRuntime ownership (fork_aspace, exec_aspace, trap page-fault dispatch).

write_sets.notes: Single-owner during initial implementation. When parallel slices fan out, each worker claims a disjoint subset (vm/structure vs vm/execution vs page_backed core vs page_backed lifecycle) via its own worktree record.

steps.title: Refresh vm-doc-gap-ledger to post-resync state
steps.notes: Captured as a dated follow-up note (2026-05-04-vm-pagebacked-gap-update.md) rather than mutating the prior 2026-05-03 ledger snapshot. Notes new useraccessif/irqif HAL surfaces and points at this plan as the new active mitigation order.

steps.title: Wire useraccessif into step_read/step_write byte transfer
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: PAGE_BACKED §5.1/5.2 byte-accurate transfer. Substrate gained a FrameKernelAddr hook (production points at the direct-map base; tests at the test direct map). Errno gained EFAULT. PageBacked exposes step_read_to_user<H: UserAccessIf> and step_write_from_user<H: UserAccessIf> in a new sibling module page_backed/user_buffer.rs (kept under the 1500-line guard) plus user_buffer_tests.rs covering single-page round trip, cross-page round trip, EFAULT propagation on read, and EFAULT propagation on write. Copyless step_read/step_write retained as the in-kernel staging surface for splice/sendfile/copy_file_range; user-buffer path routes through UserAccessIf::copy_to_user/copy_from_user.

steps.title: Implement mock FsPageBacking covering File-variant materialize_page
steps.notes: Closed as redundant. The pre-existing test mocks already cover File-variant materialize_page end-to-end: RecordingFs (page_backed.rs tests, fetch counter), BlockingFs (page_backed.rs tests, blocked outcome), and LifecycleFs (page_backed/lifecycle_tests.rs, full fetch/flush/truncate/fsync/fallocate). The fallocate slice extended LifecycleFs further. No new mock-fs-pagebacking module was needed; existing per-test mocks are sufficient for the downstream pagebacked-fallocate, partial-page-byte-fidelity, and cross-variant-scripts slices.

steps.title: Add step_fallocate for File variant
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: PAGE_BACKED §5.5. FsPageBacking gained a default-impl fallocate(fs_object_id, new_size, guard) so existing backings (RecordingFs, BlockingFs, LifecycleFs) keep compiling. step_fallocate rejects Device with EINVAL, rejects new_size beyond fixed page_count capacity with EINVAL, treats new_size <= current size as Done(()) no-op, calls FsPageBacking::fallocate first for File backings and only publishes pc.size_bytes on backing success, and bumps pc.size_bytes for Anon backings without materializing pages. Did not need a new mock-fs-pagebacking module: extending LifecycleFs with fallocates/last_fallocate_size counters and a failing_fallocate constructor was sufficient, so the original mock-fs-pagebacking prerequisite was dropped from depends_on. Five new tests cover Anon grow, File backing-first publication, File backing failure leaves state intact, Device + capacity-overflow EINVAL, and shrink/equal no-op.

steps.title: Wire PC.size into VM fault SIGBUS-style checks
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VmFaultError gained PageBeyondSize. VmFaultOutcome::materialize_page_recipe checks (page_index * USER_PAGE_SIZE) >= pc.size_bytes() before calling pc.materialize_anon and returns PageBeyondSize when the access is beyond the visible PC.size, leaving the capacity-bound BackingOffsetOverflow check intact. Three tests cover SHARED past-EOF read rejection, MAP_PRIVATE past-EOF write rejection (before CoW replacement), and admission of a page whose first byte is just below PC.size. Closes the STATUS.md 'connect PC.size to VM fault SIGBUS-style checks' next-step item.

steps.title: Byte-accurate partial-page truncate and growth
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: PAGE_BACKED §5.3 partial-page tail-zero on truncate-shrink. step_truncate now zeroes the cached partial-EOF page tail (bytes [new_size mod PAGE, PAGE_END)) after withdrawing higher pages, so a subsequent truncate-grow exposes zeros for the previously-stale region. Helper zero_partial_eof_tail uses the substrate FrameKernelAddr hook (already public from user-buffer-byte-copy slice) and is no-op when new_size is page-aligned, when the EOF page is not cached, or when the hook is missing. Read at EOF returns short count via step_read_to_user (already correct via len-clamp from user-buffer-byte-copy slice; not changed). Write at EOF grows pc.size_bytes via existing grow_size_to (also unchanged). Three tests: (1) shrink past mid-page zeroes the tail and preserves the head; (2) page-aligned shrink does not touch the surviving page; (3) end-to-end shrink-then-grow round-trip via step_read_to_user reads zeros for the post-EOF region. No full-page materialization for purely metadata growth was already the existing behavior of step_truncate-grow and step_fallocate.

steps.title: Add WaitToken → reactor::Channel resolver registry
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: Plan-extension slice. Prerequisite for the four async script wrappers (mmap-script-async, munmap-mprotect-mremap-scripts, brk-script, fault-script-async). New crate-public module crates/tx-kernel/src/wait_carrier.rs holds a SpinMutex<BTreeMap<u64, tx_reactor::wait::Channel>> registry plus an AtomicU64 carrier id allocator. register_wait_channel(channel) returns a non-zero monotonically-increasing id; release_wait_channel(id) drops the registry's clone; lookup_wait_channel(id) returns Some(Channel) if registered; wait_on_token(token) returns Some(WaitFuture) when the token's carrier is registered, None otherwise. Test placeholder tokens constructed via raw WaitToken::new(13, 0x55) safely return None from wait_on_token rather than panicking, so existing test mocks (BlockingFs, LifecycleFs) keep working unchanged. Six tests cover register/lookup/release roundtrip, distinct-ids, lookup-of-unregistered, wait_on_token round-trip, wait_on_token rejects placeholders, and wait_on_token returns None after release.

steps.title: Confirm StepOutcome carries wait tokens fault paths can yield through
steps.notes: Audit complete. StepOutcome already carries Done(T), Advanced(T), Blocked(WaitToken), AdvancedThenBlocked(T, WaitToken), and Err(Errno) per STEP_MODEL_v1 §2 five-variant algebra. WaitToken carries (carrier, interest) per §2.3 (WakeCarrier × InterestConditions). No code changes required. Convenience extractors (e.g., wait_token() helper) are deferred until the first concrete script wrapper has a real consumer; adding them now would be premature abstraction.

steps.title: Wrap resolve_fault as async fault_script with reservation drop on wait
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM_v1_2 §5.1 + §3.6 cross-async-wait discipline. AddressSpace::fault_script_async loops the three-step fault sequence: (1) acquire Materializer + observe recipe, drop reservation; (2) materialize_pagebacked (synchronous, errors propagate); (3) re-acquire Materializer + publish_fault_materialization. WouldBlock at step 1 or step 3 drops the relevant guard (and any held materialization), awaits wait_carrier::wait_on_token on the RangeLock's release token, and retries from step 1 with a fresh recipe observation. Inner sync helpers (resolve_fault, publish_fault_materialization, materialize_pagebacked) stay as the compatibility surface. Two new tests cover uncontended-one-poll-success and writer-conflict-yields-and-completes-after-release. PC-side blocking on File-variant materialize_page (FsPageBacking fetch/flush) is not yet routed through this script — that remains a follow-up requiring per-PageContainer wait channels analogous to the RangeLock channel; for v1 the script handles only the RangeLock-side blocking signal.

steps.title: Wrap mmap helpers as async mmap_script
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM_v1_2 §5.2 + §3.6 cross-async-wait discipline, end-to-end. RangeLock now owns a tx_reactor::wait::Channel registered with wait_carrier under a non-zero carrier id (pub const RANGE_LOCK_RELEASE_MASK is the mask bit fired on every release). RangeLock::release_active and release_pending_writer now fire the channel; WouldBlock<'a> carries a &'a RangeLock reference and exposes wait_token() returning a WaitToken whose carrier resolves to the lock's release channel. Drop on RangeLock releases the wait_carrier registration. AddressSpace::map_script_async is the first async script wrapper: it loops calling reserve_map; on WouldBlock, it extracts the wait_token, drops the blocked guard (releasing any pending-writer slot), awaits via wait_carrier::wait_on_token, and retries. Inner sync helpers stay as compatibility surface. Four tests in vm/tests/script_async.rs cover wait_token shape, uncontended one-poll success, blocked-then-release-wakes-and-completes, and external-subscriber wake on RangeLock release.

steps.title: Async wrappers for munmap, mprotect, mremap
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM_v1_2 §5.3/5.4/5.5 + §3.6 cross-async-wait discipline, applied via the mmap-script-async template. AddressSpace::unmap_async, AddressSpace::protect_async, and AddressSpace::remap_async each loop on their inner sync helper, drop the blocked guard on WouldBlock, await wait_carrier::wait_on_token, and retry. Inner sync helpers (unmap, protect, remap_script) stay as compatibility surface. remap_async stays in disjoint-only mode for v1 (overlapping mremap is documented v1 debt). Three new tests in vm/tests/script_async.rs cover unmap/protect/remap blocked-then-release-wakes-and-completes.

steps.title: brk_script over the existing AddressSpace mapping primitives
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM_v1_2 §5.8. AddressSpace::brk_script_async(brk_base, current_brk, requested_brk) models the program break as an Anon PrivateAnon mapping covering [brk_base, current_brk). On grow, calls map_script_async on [current_brk, requested_brk) with READ_WRITE / PRIVATE / PrivateAnon. On shrink, calls unmap_async on [requested_brk, current_brk). No-op when requested == current; rejects requested < brk_base with InvalidRange. Process-level tracking of the brk value (which hart holds it, exec-time base, fork inheritance) lives in Process and is out of scope for VM. Four tests cover grow, shrink, no-op, and below-base rejection.

steps.title: Observation-only scripts: madvise, msync, mincore
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM §5.9 observation surface. AddressSpace::mincore(range) returns range-page-count booleans against the pmap walk; AddressSpace::madvise(range, MadviseAdvice) is no-op per VM §9.7 with MadviseAdvice spelling so callers and future syscall wrappers compile against the documented enum; AddressSpace::msync(range, guard) iterates recipes overlapping range, dedups File-backed PageContainers by Cap key, and calls page_backed::step_fsync per unique PC, returning the first non-Done outcome or Done(()) if all succeed. Anon/PrivateAnon/Device backings are no-op for msync. Eight new tests in vm/tests/observation.rs cover walk_range ascending/exclusion/empty, mincore resident/absent and all-absent, madvise advice round-trip, and msync done-for-anon plus skip-anon-PC. vm/tests.rs split: observation tests moved into vm/tests/observation.rs to keep parent under the 1500-line guard.

steps.title: Extend VmPmap with walk and protect-without-teardown for mincore + future fork CoW demotion
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: Added VmPmap::walk_range(range) -> Vec<(UserPage, PmapMappingSnapshot)> for read-only enumeration used by mincore-style queries and by future fork CoW demotion to discover affected pages. Did not add a separate protect-without-teardown method; teardown_range already serves the protect-via-refault discipline per VM_v1_2 §9.8 (in-place PTE permission patching deferred). Documented teardown_range's dual role in its rustdoc. Three tests cover the walk surface: ascending order, range exclusion, and the empty case.

steps.title: Replace BTreeMap snapshot publication with persistent/epoch range index
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: VM_v1_2 §1.2 publication rule + INVARIANTS_v4 ARCH-5. RecipeIndex now publishes via AtomicPtr<RecipeTree> for lock-free reads under epoch::Guard, plus a separate writer mutation SpinMutex that serializes mutators. Writers atomically swap and retire the old tree through tx_substrate::epoch::retire_raw (now exposed publicly so upper-layer publication mechanisms can opt into EBR-managed reclamation). RecipeIndex internal read methods (lookup, stats, find_free_range, overlapping, snapshot, validate_map) take &Guard<'_> and load the tree via an internal pinned() helper that performs an Acquire load and asserts soundness via the caller's epoch guard. AddressSpace public read methods (lookup, find_free_range, recipes_overlapping, recipes_snapshot) keep their existing signatures but internally create a short-lived epoch::guard() to hand to RecipeIndex; AddressSpace::msync passes its caller-supplied guard through directly. require_map_admission grows an internal guard for validate_map. RecipeSnapshot is now cfg(test) since the publication-rule test (vm_recipe_snapshot_reader_survives_split_rewrite_publication) is its only consumer; production code reads through the borrow-under-guard path directly. Drop on RecipeIndex frees the final tree via Box::from_raw on the AtomicPtr value. Verification: 60 vm tests, 43 page_backed tests, 109 lib tests, 18 substrate page_allocator tests, fmt clean, clippy clean, all xtask lints ok, progress validate 24 ok.

steps.title: splice / sendfile / copy_file_range over PageBacked variants
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: PAGE_BACKED §9.3 copy_file_range covered by step_copy_file_range in a new sibling page_backed/cross_variant.rs module. Page-by-page copy via materialize_page on each side and the substrate FrameKernelAddr hook for direct-map byte movement. Output Device rejects EINVAL; out_offset+len beyond capacity rejects EINVAL; in_offset >= source EOF returns Done(0); the copy is clamped to in_pc.size_bytes() - in_offset; pc.size_bytes is bumped on dst only after byte progress; dirty marking is handled by materialize_page(Write) for Anon/File output. Six tests cover Anon-to-Anon within-page, page-boundary-crossing at different alignments, source-EOF-clamps-the-copy, source-at-EOF returns Done(0), Device-destination EINVAL, and dst-capacity-overflow EINVAL. Splice (§9.1) and sendfile (§9.2) are explicitly deferred: they require Pipe StructBacked which is not yet implemented; the cross_variant.rs rustdoc records this. Reflink path (§9.3 same-fs eligibility) is deferred to the reflink-cow-scaffold slice.

steps.title: Reflink + CoW-on-write scaffolding inside PageContainer share rules
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: PAGE_BACKED §7.1/§7.2. New page_backed::install_shared_page(pc, page, source_ppn) and page_backed::cow_replace_into_private(pc, page) live in a new sibling page_backed/reflink.rs module. install_shared_page acquires a fresh CachePin on source_ppn (incrementing cache_ref so the source frame stays live) and installs the entry via install_if_absent; rejects Device backings and pre-existing entries. cow_replace_into_private allocates a fresh zeroed frame, copies the cached frame's bytes via the substrate FrameCopier hook, and swaps the page-cache entry through install_if_match (which is now non-test so concurrent CoW can linearize). Existing CachePin on the old shared frame is dropped on success, decrementing its cache_ref. Six tests cover share-attaches, share-rejects-already-present, share-rejects-Device, CoW-replaces-with-matching-bytes-and-leaves-source-intact, CoW-on-missing-page errors, and CoW-rejects-Device. PageCacheIndex::install_if_match is now non-test (was cfg(test) only). Real reflink across two RNodes (filesystem-side) and the §12.4 reflink-vs-truncate race remain deferred to backends and follow-up slices.

steps.title: Implement AddressSpace::fork_aspace per VM_v1_2 §5.6
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes:
Plan-extension closing the VM_v1_2 §5.6 gap missed in the original plan. AddressSpace::fork_aspace(parent) -> Result snapshots parent's recipes (cheap clone via Cap refcount bumps for VmBacking::Page entries), constructs a fresh child AddressSpace via new_for_platform::

, commits each parent recipe into the child via RecipeIndex::commit_map(_, RequireFree), and tears down parent's pmap on every MAP_PRIVATE entry so subsequent writes refault and the existing materialize_page_recipe CoW path produces a private frame. MAP_SHARED PTEs in parent are left intact; child's pmap starts empty and rebuilds via refault. V1 caller invariant per §9.5: no other VM operation runs against parent during fork (Process subsystem serializes externally). Two tests cover recipe-clone-shape parity and MAP_PRIVATE-only PTE demotion.

steps.title: Implement AddressSpace::exec_aspace teardown per VM_v1_2 §5.7
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: Plan-extension closing the VM_v1_2 §5.7 gap missed in the original plan. AddressSpace::teardown_all_pmap iterates every recipe range and calls VmPmap::teardown_range, returning the page count. AddressSpace::exec_aspace is the script-side wrapper. Recipe-tree management remains caller-side because the new image's recipe shape comes from the exec image loader (Process-side, not yet implemented); v1 callers either drop the AddressSpace entirely or follow with explicit recipe modifications. Caller invariant per §5.7 prologue: exec has reduced the thread group to one; no concurrent VM operations exist on old_aspace. One test covers all-PTEs-torn-down on an Anon mapping after baseline fault publication.

steps.title: Polish: rename acquire to acquire_step + add UserRange::full_user_v1 + fork serializes via full_user lock
verification: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings
steps.notes: Audit follow-up. (1) RangeLock::acquire and acquire_pair renamed to acquire_step and acquire_pair_step to match VM_v1_2 §3.1 spelling. AcquireResult / AcquirePairResult retained as a 2-variant Result-shaped enum because the doc's StepOutcome<RangeGuard> is semantically equivalent and the rename to StepOutcome would ripple into the broader StepOutcome integration which is its own concern. All callers updated mechanically (vm/execution.rs, vm/tests.rs, vm/tests/fault_materialization.rs, vm/tests/script_async.rs). (2) New constant types::FULL_USER_V1_TOP = 1 << 38 and method UserRange::full_user_v1() returning the [0, FULL_USER_V1_TOP) range. Sized to fit inside Sv39 (256 GiB user) and Sv48 (128 TiB user) user-space halves. (3) AddressSpace::fork_aspace now acquires ExclusiveWriter on full_user_v1 before snapshotting parent recipes, satisfying VM_v1_2 §9.5 fork-serializes-parent. WouldBlock returns VmMapError::WouldBlock; callers retry. One new test fork_aspace_returns_would_block_when_parent_full_user_range_already_held confirms the lock fires.

steps.title: Final ledger + STATUS update; verify completion bar
steps.notes: Restate completion at >=85% on structure and behavior. Name remaining gaps explicitly: fork_aspace/exec_aspace/trap-dispatch (Process-blocked), reclaim policy and writeback scheduling (v1-deferred), reverse mapping/hugetlb/userfaultfd/in-place-mprotect/mlock optimization (deferred). verification.command: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-qemu-virt --exclude tx-kernel-riscv64-m1dock-mock --exclude tx-kernel-loongarch64-qemu-virt -- -D warnings

risks: wait-aware-step-outcome may force StepOutcome shape changes that ripple into reactor and other subsystems; keep the change narrow and additive.
persistent-epoch-recipes is a foundational rewrite; it can land in parallel with script wrappers but conflicts with vm/checks staged witnesses must be resolved deliberately.
user-buffer-byte-copy depends on the host-test side of useraccessif; if the host harness lacks a usable mock, add one before tightening byte-equality assertions.
Each script wrapper risks duplicating reservation/revalidation logic; factor a shared helper once two wrappers exist.
blockers: fork_aspace, exec_aspace, and trap page-fault dispatch are explicitly out of scope: they require Process ownership of Cap<AddressSpace> and ThreadRuntime authority paths.
Concrete VFS backends (ext4, devfs, bdev-fs) are out of scope; mock FsPageBacking is the substitute.
PAGE_BACKED §8 reclaim policy and §12 open questions are deferred by the design docs.
